first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A planning service with a 'Wedded Advisor' who helps you pick a region and venue in Portugal and sort the legal paperwork. The top is mostly a Portugal fact sheet: palaces, cliffs, one month for paperwork, avoid July and August. No price anywhere in sight, which is the first thing I look for.

attention_map.quote: Wedded Concierge pairs you with a Wedded Advisor who plans with you from the first enquiry to the last dance.
attention_map.why: Four lines of travel facts and a slogan. Tells me what Portugal is, not what you charge or what you have done. Kept going only because the facts were specific, not fluffy.

attention_map.quote: Legal and travel details from official sources, including IRN, GOV.UK and Smartraveller.
attention_map.why: Naming sources is the kind of thing I can check. Good sign.

attention_map.section: Fall for Portugal Before You Choose a Venue
attention_map.quote: The legacy of Ferdinand II, the King-Artist: a coloured, castle-like palace crowning the Sintra hills in a wooded park.
attention_map.why: Reads like the palace's own tourist blurb. Nice, but it is brochure stuff I can get from the palace website. Nothing about your weddings there.

attention_map.quote: We group Portugal wedding venues into five regions, each with its own setting, served by four airports.
attention_map.why: I counted: five region cards (Lisbon/Sintra/Cascais, Algarve, Porto/Douro, Comporta/Alentejo, Madeira) and four airports (LIS, FAO, OPO, FNC). It matches here, in Getting There and in FAQ 6. That is the first thing that made me trust the page a bit.

attention_map.quote: state events can cancel bookings at Queluz or the National Palace of Sintra; nothing may be fixed to the heritage.
attention_map.why: Finally a catch stated up front. The five Parques de Sintra venues and the Monserrate roof works to first quarter 2027 are repeated the same way in the hero caption, the card and FAQ 10. Consistent.

attention_map.section: See Why Couples Marry in Portugal
attention_map.quote: a destination wedding in Portugal gives couples five things in one country.
attention_map.why: Third time I am told about Sintra palaces, Douro UNESCO terraces and Algarve clifftops. Same facts, new heading. Feels like padding.

attention_map.section: What Your Wedded Advisor Checks in Every Venue Contract
attention_map.quote: exclusive use can mean paying for rooms your guests do not fill.
attention_map.why: This is the most useful box on the page for me: buy-out vs venue fee, per day vs per guest, VAT. It admits the hidden costs exist. But it only tells me where the costs hide, not how much they are.

attention_map.section: Plan Your Portugal Wedding, Step by Step: Entry rules and Marrying legally
attention_map.quote: Submit at least one month before your date. The registrar agrees the date, time and place; a ceremony away from the registry or out of hours is agreed in advance.
attention_map.why: Detailed, sourced, dated 'checked October 2026'. The one month rule matches the hero, the legal card and FAQs 1, 5 and 9. Useful, but this is government info, not proof you can deliver a wedding.

attention_map.section: What a Wedding in Portugal Costs
attention_map.quote: What a wedding in Portugal costs depends on five things: your guest count, the region, the season, how many nights you take the venue and whether you book it for exclusive use. We talk you through the options for your plans.
attention_map.why: A heading that promises costs and then gives zero numbers. Not even a range. FAQ 4 says the same: 'There is no single average'. This is exactly 'call us for a price', which is what I am trying to avoid. The other tabs I have open will show something.

attention_map.section: See What a Portugal Wedding Weekend Includes
attention_map.quote: There is no set Portugal package: every weekend is built to your plan. We help you shape it around your guests, and it can include:
attention_map.why: The heading says 'Includes' but the list is 'can include'. That is a menu, not an inclusions list. No price against any of it, no exclusions. Is the on-the-day coordinator part of your fee or extra?

attention_map.section: Bring Your Guests, or Keep It Exclusive to You
attention_map.quote: Build a guest website in Wonderland Studio: share the schedule, travel and entry rules in one place. Start for free
attention_map.why: 'Start for free' makes me ask what the paid version is. Feels like a side product slipped in.

attention_map.section: Celebrate More Than a Wedding in Portugal
attention_map.quote: Renew your vows on an Algarve clifftop above the Atlantic.
attention_map.why: Not relevant to me, and the images repeat the same clifftop, Douro and Pena shots again.

attention_map.section: Plan Your Portugal Wedding with One Wedded Advisor
attention_map.quote: When you plan with Wedded Concierge, your advisor explains what the programme offers for your dates.
attention_map.why: 'Wedded Privileges' with no content at all. What is the programme? What does it cost? What does the advisor cost? If the service is free, who pays you, and does that mean you steer me to certain venues? This is the catch I am looking for and the page is silent.

attention_map.quote: Budget, dates you have in mind, anything else
attention_map.why: You want my budget but will not show me yours. Form is long (eleven fields) for someone who has not seen a single number.

attention_map.quote: Yes, a beach wedding in Portugal is possible with a permit. On designated bathing beaches, the local council licenses events under Decree-Law 97/2018
attention_map.why: Specific and consistent with the Algarve card. FAQ 4 on cost is the weak one, the rest is solid.

attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding / Ronaldo and Georgina's intimate Portugal wedding
attention_map.why: Two links to what looks like the same celebrity story, under a label 'Trending row' that looks like it was left in by mistake. Celebrity gossip is not proof you have done a wedding. Looks sloppy.

questions_answered.question: What is NOT included in the from price?
questions_answered.evidence: There is no from price at all. 'There is no set Portugal package' and 'it can include' a list with no prices and no exclusions. The contract box names cost traps (rooms, buy-out, per guest, VAT) but gives no figures.

questions_answered.question: Are these facts consistent across the page?
questions_answered.evidence: Five regions and four airports match in the region intro, the legal card, Getting There and FAQ 6. Five Parques de Sintra venues match in the hero caption, the palace card, the booking box and FAQ 10. One month lead time and Monserrate roof works to first quarter 2027 repeat identically. Only small wobble: 'Clifftop or beach. Atlantic views on the Algarve and the west coast' while elsewhere clifftops are only the Algarve.

questions_answered.question: What proof is there that this team has done this venue before?
questions_answered.evidence: No real weddings, no couple quotes, no named venues you have worked with, no numbers of weddings planned. The only 'stories' are celebrity weddings in the 'Trending row'. The images are all placeholders and nothing is captioned as one of your weddings.

questions_answered.question: Why book through you and not the venue directly?
questions_answered.evidence: 'Your advisor is your one contact at Wedded Concierge, instead of one conversation per venue' and they 'check each venue contract before you sign'. That is a reason, but nothing on what it costs me or whether it is cheaper or dearer than going direct.

questions_answered.question: What happens if something goes wrong on the day?
questions_answered.evidence: Only 'An on-the-day coordinator' in a 'can include' list, plus 'We check the terms with you before you book' for palace cancellations. No wet weather plan, no backup, no word on who is responsible if a supplier lets us down.

objections_triggered.objection: No price and no inclusions list means hidden costs
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'What a Wedding in Portugal Costs' section with no numbers; 'There is no single average'; 'it can include'
'plans with you from the first enquiry to the last dance' with no real weddings, reviews or venue track record anywhere on the page

objections_triggered.objection: Unknown cost of the concierge itself (what's the catch)
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'Wedded Privileges ... your advisor explains what the programme offers for your dates.' and no mention of a fee or who pays the advisor
'Trending row' label and two near-identical Ronaldo and Georgina links

objections_triggered.objection: Venue blurbs read like they are copied from the palace's own site
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'The legacy of Ferdinand II, the King-Artist: a coloured, castle-like palace crowning the Sintra hills'
Checked regions, airports, palace count, lead times, roof works dates: not triggered

trust_signals_noticed: Named official sources with links (IRN, Justica, GOV.UK, US State Department, Smartraveller, embassies)
Consistent numbers across the page: five regions, four airports, five Parques de Sintra venues, one month lead time
Catches stated openly: state events can cancel Queluz or National Palace of Sintra bookings; Monserrate roof works until first quarter 2027
Contract checklist naming real cost traps: rooms and exclusivity, buy-out vs venue fee, per day vs per guest, VAT
'We confirm the transfer time for each venue' instead of promising one
turn_offs_noticed: Mild slogan rather than superlatives: 'from the first enquiry to the last dance'
Celebrity 'Trending row' with a duplicated Ronaldo link
The same Sintra, Douro and Algarve facts repeated in three separate sections
No urgency tactics, which I appreciated

images.stopped_on: None really. The closest was the hero caption 'Pena, Sintra: Ferdinand II's palace above its wooded park, one of five heritage venues hired out by Parques de Sintra' because it carried a checkable number.
felt_generic_or_stock: wedded-advisor-planning-with-couple.jpg: reads like a stock 'planner with happy couple' shot, says nothing about who your advisors are
images.repetition: Pena or Sintra palace appears about five times, Douro terraces about six, Algarve clifftops about six. After the second section it feels like the same three photos on loop.
images.missing: Not one image captioned as a wedding you actually planned.

emotional_response.overall: Cautiously impressed by the homework, frustrated by the silence on money.
emotional_response.trust: I trust the legal info. I do not yet trust the company, because I have seen nothing it has done.
emotional_response.fear_of_upsell: Raised, not calmed. 'Can include', 'programme', 'Start for free' and 'we talk you through the options' all point to a sales call where the price appears later.

payload.decision_reason: The page answers Portugal's paperwork better than my other tabs, but it answers none of the money questions: no price, no from price, no inclusions or exclusions, and nothing on what the advisor costs. There is also zero proof this team has run a wedding at any of these venues. My rule is no enquiry while a cost question is open, and here every cost question is open. I will take the legal steps with me and compare against planners who show a number.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Okay, credit where it's due, the numbers add up. Five regions, four airports, five Sintra palaces, one month for the paperwork, and they say it the same way every time. They even tell me a state event can bump my palace booking. But then I hit 'What a Wedding in Portugal Costs' and there's not one dollar figure in it. 'There is no single average.' Right. 'See what a weekend includes' and it's a 'can include' list. And what's the catch with the advisor? Who pays them? 'Wedded Privileges' is one sentence that says nothing. No real weddings, no reviews, just Ronaldo twice under something called 'Trending row'. They want my budget in the form but won't show me theirs. I've got three other tabs open that at least give me a ballpark. I'm out.
